title: Wing Lower Cover Panel — External Bonded Repair Patch for Thinned Material Near a Tank Access Cut-Out

issue.reason: Issue B. Earlier issues are not held in this dataset.

ata.title: Wing Box Structure — Lower Cover Panels

abstract: External bonded repair patch on the wing lower shell near a tank access cut-out, used where material has been lost to corrosion under a weeping panel edge and the remaining thickness is below the blend limit.

sections.purpose: This repair restores the static strength and the fatigue capability of the wing lower cover panel after material has been removed to clean up corrosion around a tank access cut-out.
sections.damage_assessment: Clean the area around the cut-out and remove the sealant fillet. Map the remaining thickness on a 25 millimetre grid by ultrasonic measurement and record the thinnest reading. Damage inside the blend limit does not need this repair. Damage that reaches the cut-out edge land, damage that crosses a stringer run-out, or damage within 60 millimetres of an existing repair is outside the scope. Where the corrosion has been caused by a weeping panel, inspect the internal face of the cut-out land as well; corrosion on both faces changes the repair from a patch to a panel assessment. Record the fuel tank entry history for the panel if the operator maintains it, because a repeated weep at the same panel usually means the closure and not the panel is the problem.
sections.repair_procedure: Rout the damaged material to a smooth oval with a minimum corner radius of 15 millimetres and blend the edges to a 20 to 1 ratio. Do a dye penetrant inspection of the routed edge and confirm that no indication remains. Machine the recess to the depth on repair drawing RD-57-10-12-913 so that the patch sits flush and does not stand into the airflow. Prepare the bonding surfaces to the finish on sheet 2 and apply the chromate-free protection to all bare material. Cut the patch from the sheet stock on the drawing and check its fit dry. Apply the adhesive film, position the patch and cure it under vacuum with the heater blanket, monitoring the skin temperature throughout; where the low temperature cure system has been released for this scheme it may be used instead. Install the perimeter fasteners wet with sealant, working from the centre outwards, using the clip D5710128621379 at the two positions that land on the stringer flange. Restore the sealant fillet at the cut-out and the external finish to smoothness class A.
sections.inspection_requirements: Do a tap test of the full patch area and an ultrasonic inspection of the bond line every 5000 flight cycles. Do a detailed visual inspection of the patch perimeter and of the cut-out sealant fillet at every tank entry. Any disbond larger than 100 square millimetres, any new corrosion inside the repair boundary, or any fuel weep at the patch edge makes the repair invalid. The repair is life limited to 16000 flight cycles from the date of embodiment.

type_data.allowable_damage_limits: Material loss up to 18 per cent of the nominal panel thickness over an area not larger than 140 by 90 millimetres, not reaching the cut-out edge land, not crossing a stringer run-out and not closer than 60 millimetres to an existing repair.

type_data.fastener_pattern: Single perimeter row, 48 fasteners, 22 mm pitch, 16 mm edge distance, with a doubled row at the cut-out side
type_data.fatigue_life_note: Repair is life limited to 16000 flight cycles; a bond line ultrasonic inspection is required every 5000 flight cycles.
